flags.source_says: PDF keys (c) 'Settlement positions' and adds an errata note claiming the published AnalystPrep Q.3916 key 'other cash transactions' is wrong (PDF p.44-45).
flags.derivation: In the reading (LR Ch. 6 Intraday Liquidity Risk Management, tracking-intraday-flows measures), the measure 'Other cash transactions' is itself defined as: firms should track intraday and end-of-day settlement positions at all FMUs in which they participate, maximising transaction-level detail and capturing the data for analysis. The stem paraphrases exactly that definition. 'Settlement positions' is not a named measure in the reading at all (the list is total payments, other cash transactions, time-sensitive obligations, total intraday credit lines to clients and counterparties, total bank intraday credit lines available and usage). So the original AnalystPrep key (b) was right and the PDF's errata inverted a correct key. The JSON's definition of 'other cash transactions' ('internal book transfers and non-payment cash activity') is not in the reading; it was invented to support the errata. Same item exists as LR-T3-16 (key c) and needs the same fix.
flags.evidence: PDF p.45 errata: 'The published answer to this item is other cash transactions. That is inconsistent with the stem...'. Contradicted by notes/FRM_Consolidated_Vol2/ch/41_LR_LTR6.tex lines ~96-136 (LTR-6 c table: 'Measures for tracking intraday flows' = Total payments; Other cash transactions - 'track intraday and end-of-day settlement positions at all FMUs'; Time-sensitive obligations; Total intraday credit lines to clients and counterparties; Total bank intraday credit lines available and usage. 'Measures for quantifying and monitoring risk levels' = Daily maximum intraday liquidity usage; Intraday credit relative to Tier 1 capital; Client intraday credit usage; Payment throughput)

flags.proposed: Replace the table with the reading's flow-tracking measures: Total payments | payer and payee information, payment system used, time received or originated, routing information, suspensions and credit status of each payment; Other cash transactions | intraday and end-of-day settlement positions at all FMUs in which the bank participates, captured at transaction level for analysis; Time-sensitive obligations | transactions that must settle by a specific time of day; Total intraday credit lines to clients and counterparties; Total bank intraday credit lines available and usage. Replace 'The stem matches the third row word for word: settlement positions...' with 'The stem matches the definition of other cash transactions word for word: settlement positions at every FMU, at transaction level. The name is counter-intuitive, which is exactly why it is tested: the measure is labelled other cash transactions but is organised by venue (the FMU).' Delete any statement that settlement positions is a separate named measure.

flags.proposed: Key (d) is defensible, but the data and reporting component explicitly includes 'regular liquidity reporting, possibly daily'. To remove overlap, reword (d) to e.g. 'Business-as-usual funds transfer pricing, being the allocation of day-to-day funding costs to business lines.' or keep (d) and add the distinction in the solution (see solution flag).
flags.derivation: Reading's data and reporting component: timely and accurate data on the liquidity position is essential; regular liquidity reporting, possibly daily, is desirable. A candidate who knows the five components could argue (d) describes part of that component, so an EXCEPT answer relying on 'daily liquidity position reporting is not part of the plan' is shaky.

flags.current: 'A sound structure has three elements, and the third is the one most often missing in practice.' Table: Active risk management = real-time monitoring; Risk assessment = formal identification and measurement; Integration with risk governance = risk appetite, limit framework and committee structure.
flags.proposed: 'The reading lists four characteristics of an effective governance structure; option B names three of them.' Table: Active risk management | intraday liquidity risk is actively managed rather than accepted as a cost of doing business, with settlement and systemic risks classified in the risk taxonomy and built into the risk appetite framework; Risk assessment | treated as a component of risk self-assessments; Integration with risk governance | the three lines of defence: treasury, risk management and internal audit; Risk measurement and monitoring | intraday credit extended to clients and intraday credit the bank uses itself. Key (b) unchanged.
flags.derivation: The reading's governance characteristics are four (active risk management, risk assessment, integration with risk governance, risk measurement and monitoring), and integration means the three-lines-of-defence structure, while risk-appetite incorporation belongs to active risk management. Key unaffected since (b) is the only sound option.
